title: Scott's Terra Nova expedition to the South Pole
summary: The British Antarctic Expedition under Robert Falcon Scott left London on 1 June 1910 and set out for the Pole on 1 November 1911. Scott's party of five reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912 and found that Amundsen's Norwegian party had arrived 34 days earlier. All five died on the return journey; Scott's last diary entry is dated 29 March 1912.

uncertainty.note: Gazette title gives 1910 to 1913. Polar journey 1 November 1911 to March 1912; the bodies were found 12 November (1912). The nzaht page puts Amundsen's arrival 35 days earlier, the Gazette 34.

reviewer_note: Only the 1 November 1911 start, 17 January 1912 Pole, 17 February Evans death and 29 March last diary entry are dated on opened pages; Scott's own death date is not stated (29 March is the presumed date per the Gazette). The Beardmore waypoint is the glacier centre point, not the death site, and Cape Evans as the departure point is inferred from the base-camp wording.

beats.caption: Scott leaves base on 1 November 1911 with support parties, motor sledges, dogs and ponies.
The party of five reaches the South Pole on 17 January 1912 and finds a Norwegian tent already there.
On the return Edgar Evans dies on 17 February; Scott's last diary entry is dated 29 March, and none of the five survives.
